intent.purpose: Source of truth for all adopted governance frameworks and their implementing artifacts
intent.scope: Framework entries and pending adoptions only. NOT the adoption process (framework-adoption.md). NOT framework documentation (framework-*.md files)

frameworks.name: Three-layer governance
frameworks.governs: Prevention, detection, and audit of all harness activity

frameworks.name: Incident governance
frameworks.governs: Tracking and resolving harness deficiencies with root cause analysis and corrective actions

frameworks.name: Tool lifecycle
frameworks.governs: Evaluation, approval, integration, maintenance, and health tracking of managed tools

frameworks.name: Managed file deployment
frameworks.governs: Deploying and reconciling harness content across machines

frameworks.name: Incident investigation
frameworks.governs: Root cause analysis and corrective actions when something goes wrong

frameworks.name: Framework adoption
frameworks.governs: How the harness grows by adopting concepts from established disciplines

frameworks.name: Intent documentation
frameworks.governs: Every file and section states its purpose, scope, and audience

frameworks.name: Governed data access
frameworks.governs: Access control for governed JSON registries — skill-gated process enforcement
frameworks.discipline: Information security, quality management, software engineering

frameworks.name: Artifact harvesting
frameworks.governs: Lifecycle of reusable artifacts produced during sessions — code, prompts, patterns, research

frameworks.name: Tool operations
frameworks.governs: Per-tool operational metadata, governance modes, and verification specs for deeply-integrated managed tools

frameworks.name: Adversarial review
frameworks.governs: Attacking a draft in thinking before it is written to a file, until the attacks find nothing to fix (prompt-turn checklist item 8)
frameworks.discipline: Military and intelligence analysis (red teaming, structured analytic techniques)
concepts: Red teaming (UK MOD Red Teaming Handbook, 3rd ed., 2021)
Key assumptions check (US Government Tradecraft Primer, 2009)

frameworks.name: Perspective-based reading
frameworks.governs: Reviewing a written file once per reader, each pass from one reader's perspective with that reader's questions (prompt-turn checklist item 9)
concepts: Perspective-based reading (Basili et al., Empirical Software Engineering, 1996)
Perspective-specific questions (Shull, Rus, Basili, IEEE Computer, 2000)

frameworks.name: Mission command
frameworks.governs: Fixing the meaning of an order before acting, and resolving what you can on your own initiative within the commander's intent, reporting every deviation (prompt-turn checklist items 2 and 4)
frameworks.discipline: Military command and control (mission command; Auftragstaktik)
concepts: Auftragstaktik / Führen mit Auftrag (Joint Force Quarterly 96, 2020; Handbuch Innere Führung, 2023)

frameworks.name: Request for information
frameworks.governs: Raising what an agent cannot resolve, and what it finds, to the commander as numbered session RFIs with a suggested answer (prompt-turn checklist item 5)
frameworks.discipline: Construction contract administration; military intelligence doctrine
concepts: RFI numbered, logged and tracked (AIA G716-2004)
Ask only what research cannot answer

pending.name: Artifact registry
pending.governs: Inventory and dependency graph of all source artifacts — kind, intent, governance status, and managed-tool / inter-artifact dependencies; derived (generated) from in-file metadata, not hand-authored
pending.discipline: Configuration management (ITIL CMDB), Software supply chain (SBOM)
